edge_explainer.market_believes: The Michael Kors turnaround is on track: deleveraged post-Versace-sale, a $921M buyback (~43% of the market cap), and a guided EPS inflection to ~$2.15 — the market prices ~74% odds the inflection works.
edge_explainer.we_believe: We put the odds LOWER (~65%): the filed numbers show Michael Kors constant-currency revenue RE-WIDENING (-8.4%, worse than two quarters ago), zero of the seven signals that marked Coach's real turnaround, and last quarter's 'return to profitability' was substantially a one-time $40M tariff refund.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: This is a case where our estimate says the market is TOO OPTIMISTIC — so the honest conclusion is no long edge at $18.5. Our work here protects capital rather than deploys it.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: It's the reverse: the inflection is OVER-priced. The mechanical EPS floor (interest income + buyback ≈ $1.50-1.65) limits the downside, which is why it's a skip rather than a short.
edge_explainer.what_resolves_it: Q1 FY27 print (~early Aug, unconfirmed) and, decisively, whether Michael Kors' revenue decline NARROWS by Q2. Re-look only at $15-16.5.
edge_explainer.edge_type: none at this price — the edge is the EXCLUSION
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: Our too-optimistic-market read dies if MK constant-currency revenue decline NARROWS by Q2 FY27 — then the market's 74% inflection odds were right and our 65% was the miscalibration.
